_how_to_edit: Replace these placeholder people with your own family and friends.
Every suspect needs a name, a pronoun (he, she or they) and a value for every trait.
No two people may have the same pronoun AND identical traits, or the crime computer can't tell them apart.
Values work best as short phrases that several people share: two people with red hair, three who love karaoke, and so on.
You can rename, add or remove traits. Each trait's clues are witness sentences; {value} becomes that person's value.
In sentences use {They}/{they}, {Them}/{them}, {Their}/{their} and stick to verbs that work for he, she and they (simple past tense is safest: 'had', 'kept', 'ordered').
bio and catchphrase are optional. The catchphrase is what they say when you catch them.

witness_pronouns: true means witnesses say he/she/they and the crime computer has a Pronoun field (like the original game). If someone is the only 'they' or the only 'she', that gives them away, so set it to false and every witness says 'they'.

traits.label: Hobby
clues: {They} asked if there was anywhere nearby for {value}.
{They} said {they} never missed a weekend of {value}.

traits.label: Favourite food
clues: {They} asked where to get the best {value} in town.
